newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO denies poaching Deutsche UK team.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO denies poaching Deutsche UK team.

text.p: Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV on Wednesday denied it had tried to poach a team of fund managers from Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London.

But ABN AMRO chief spokesman Jules Prast declined to say if the Dutch bank had tried to hire Nicola Horlick, one of the most powerful fund managers in the City of London, from Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM).

London's Financial Times newspaper said Horlick was suspended on Tuesday pending a probe into allegations she breached her contract by trying to lure colleagues to ABN AMRO, which is expanding its fund management activities in London.
"We are surprised to be mentioned in the context of poaching which would, by its nature, imply you are planning to take a whole team, which we are not," Prast told Reuters.
"When it comes down to talking to individual people, you are not talking about poaching," he said.
But he said preferred not to discuss whether ABN AMRO had or planned to talk to Horlick, the 35-year-old head of MGAM's pension fund business, the investment banking arm of Germany's Deutsche Bank.
"We never comment on who we are talking to before anything is concluded," he added.
British media have portrayed Horlick as a high-flier who has combined a successful million-stg per year career with the role of mother of five children.
ABN AMRO's Asset Management UK unit, launched in the last two years, specialises in discretionary funds management for professionals, but hopes to expand into other areas.
